claims.body: The Senators have been near the top of the league at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Sharks one of the worst. story.head: The Senators should drive the play
paras: The Sharks won the teams’ first meeting this season, 6-2 in Ottawa on Oct 22. The Senators (8-5-1) lost 6-5 in overtime to Los Angeles on Thursday, while the Sharks (7-6-1) beat Vancouver 3-2 the same night. Going in, the Sens are fifth in the Atlantic (tied for tenth in the NHL) and the Sharks fourth in the Pacific (tied for 16th).

The Senators’ record (.607) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.531), largely thanks to pulling off wins in one-goal games. So is the Sharks’ (.536 on chances worth .386), largely thanks to their goaltending.

The Senators draw more penalties than they take (2nd), rarely get pinned in their own end (2nd) and play slow, tight games (3rd lowest). As for the Sharks, they do a lot of their shooting from distance (3rd lowest) and ice the puck a lot (32nd). Both teams like to hit, especially the Sharks (2nd), so expect plenty of it. Beyond that, the Senators keep dangerous shots away, but the Sharks give up a lot of them.

Tim Stützle (8 G / 11 A / 19 P in 14 GP) leads the Senators in scoring and is tied for tenth in the NHL, with seven points in his last five games. Drake Batherson (8 G / 8 A / 16 P in 14 GP) isn’t far behind, with ten points in his last five games and a point in five straight games against San Jose. The Sharks’ scoring runs through Macklin Celebrini (5 G / 11 A / 16 P in 12 GP), and Will Smith (6 G / 4 A / 10 P in 14 GP) has a team-high six goals.
Jonas Johansson (1-1-0 / .859 SV% in 3 GS) is expected to start for Ottawa, and Yaroslav Askarov (4-5-0 / .900 SV% in 9 GS) for San Jose.
The Senators usually control more of the chances than the Sharks do.

The Sharks are newly without Igor Chernyshov, and have been without Alexander Wennberg since Oct 19.
Tim Stützle has eight goals on chances worth about 4.0 goals, well above what his finishing usually turns chances into. Runs like that tend to cool off.
